Parity assertions for research/plan/implement, all enumerated inputs
Negative assertions: --clean, no --lit, no empty tags, model emptiness

approaches_tried.approach: Copy full skill-base.sh/manifest-routing-lib.sh/continuation-pointer-lib.sh into an isolated fixture repo (test-skill-base-lifecycle.sh's pattern)
approaches_tried.reason: Discovered the SUT's SKILL_REPO_ROOT is honored from an already-exported env var (skill-base.sh's ${SKILL_REPO_ROOT:-...} default pattern), so only the three ${SKILL_REPO_ROOT}-qualified collaborator scripts (memory-retrieve.sh, literature-lit-flag-resolve.sh, literature-briefing-invoke.sh) needed fixture stubs; the SUT's own skill-base.sh/lib/*.sh neighbors resolve to their real, unmodified copies via SCRIPT_DIR -- a much lighter fixture.

notes: Regression-bite check performed manually (not part of the permanent suite): removed the implement-phase plan_path gatherer line from a scratch copy, swapped it into the deployed script location, re-ran the suite (48 passed / 1 failed, exactly the removed gatherer's assertion), then restored the original and re-ran (49 passed / 0 failed). Confirms the parity test actually bites.

Fixing this phase's own new lib dependency (continuation-pointer-lib.sh) exposed that test-orchestrate-triage-classify.sh's isolated sandbox fixture did not copy the new library file, and that two deploy-integration tests (test-deploy-orphans.sh, test-deploy-propagation.sh) hand-author a scratch .gitignore fixture that needed the new **/.dispatch/ line added alongside the other three ephemeral patterns. All three were fixed as part of this phase's own full-suite gate (bash .claude/scripts/tests/run-all.sh went from 59 passed/3 failed to 62 passed/0 failed).
